analysis.title: Nvidia Corp. (NVDA): Strong outlook despite uncertainty, with steady commitment to balancing shareholder returns and ecosystem support
key_insights: Nvidia reported 3Q26 revenue of $115.8bn vs GS $110.1bn and Street $109.5bn. Data Center revenue was $107.6bn vs GS $102.6bn and Street $102.0bn. Edge Computing revenue was $8.2bn vs $7.5bn for GS and the Street.

Nvidia raised its CY27 (FY28) revenue growth forecast to 75% from 70%, after accounting for newly issued US Department of Commerce restrictions on datacenter rentals by Nvidia's customers to restricted geographies including mainland China. GS had 74% and the Street 70%.

Rubin product revenue was about $20bn in its first quarter shipping in production. Management says unconstrained CY27 demand growth remains well in excess of supply. GS attributes demand to new customer cohorts (AI labs, neoclouds, sovereigns) in addition to hyperscalers.

Management transition: co-founder Jensen Huang resigned and Colette Kress is Interim CEO. The Board is considering internal and external candidates, has retained Heidrick & Struggles, and set no timeframe. Chairman Harvey Jones said on the call the Board does not intend to reinstate Huang as CEO.

Nvidia's financial commitments to customers and supply chain partners total $518bn, up from $366bn last quarter. Supply chain and capacity commitments are $390bn (from $279bn), cloud service agreements $28bn (from $29bn), datacenter leases $74bn (from $25bn), equity investments $20bn (from $25bn) and CapEx $6bn (from $8bn). Neocloud-specific commitments total $32bn.

Nvidia said it intends to return all excess cash to shareholders, with about $227bn of remaining buyback authorization to be executed before the end of CY27. GS reads this as management viewing the stock as significantly undervalued.

Export controls: Nvidia sees upside to its prior CY27 forecast despite the new Commerce restriction, is cooperating with all government investigations on export controls, created a Board-level National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee, and no longer ships permissible Hopper products to China.

4Q26 guidance: revenue $130bn at the midpoint vs GS and Street at $124.8bn. Non-GAAP gross margin guided to 71.5% vs GS 72.2% and Street 71.5%. OpEx $10.7bn, non-GAAP tax rate 17%. Implied non-GAAP EPS is $2.81 vs GS $2.88 and Street $2.67. FY4Q is a 14-week quarter.
Balance sheet working capital rose in 3Q: inventory $39.7bn (+26% QoQ) with days of inventory at 124 (up 4 days), and accounts receivable $81.0bn (+29% QoQ) with DSO at 64 days (up 4 days).

GS retains Buy and a $220 12-month price target, based on 22x P/E on normalized EPS of $10.00. GS expects the stock's multiple to be affected more than earnings by uncertainty, and notes NVDA had already traded at a wide discount to the market on concern that AI infrastructure growth could slow without financing from Nvidia or its competitors.

GS raised EPS estimates by an average of 4%. CY26 EPS goes to $9.65 from $9.40, CY27 to $18.00 from $16.70, CY28 to $23.10 from $23.00. The 4Q guide is read as most constructive for Broadcom, AMD, Marvell, ARM and Intel.
GS expects the stock to hold its gains, set against neutral-to-negative investor positioning based on its client conversations.

market_movers.rationale: GS retains Buy on favorable risk/reward over 12-18 months despite management transition and investigations. The $220 target is 22x normalized EPS of $10.00 and implies 39.9% upside to the report's price basis.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 (reported 11/17): revenue $115.8bn vs GS $110.1bn and Street $109.5bn. Revenue grew 20.4% QoQ and 103.2% YoY.
3Q26 reported non-GAAP EPS $2.68 vs GS est $2.57 and Street consensus $2.44 (+4.3% vs GS, +9.7% vs Street).
3Q26 gross margin including SBC 74.9% reported vs GS est 74.1% and Street est 73.5%. Operating margin 67.2% reported vs GS est 67.4% and Street est 64.8%.
3Q26 Data Center revenue $107.6bn reported vs GS est $102.6bn and Street est $102.0bn. Edge Computing revenue $8.2bn reported vs GS est $7.5bn and Street est $7.5bn.

4Q26 guidance (company, midpoint): revenue $130bn (range $120.9bn to $133.9bn) vs GS est $124.8bn and Street est $124.8bn. Non-GAAP gross margin 71.5% vs GS est 72.2% and Street est 71.5%. Implied non-GAAP EPS $2.81 (GS calculation from guidance) vs GS est $2.88 and Street est $2.67.

GS estimates (not company guidance): CY26 EPS $9.65, CY27 EPS $18.00, CY28 EPS $23.10. CY26 revenue $426.1bn, CY27 $759.6bn, CY28 $957.1bn. Quarterly GS EPS estimates: 4Q (Jan-27) $2.88, 1Q (Apr-27) $3.42, 2Q (Jul-27) $4.09.
Company CY27 (FY28) revenue growth forecast of 75%, raised from 70% prior, compared with GS prior expectation of 74% and Street at 70%.
risk_factors: Ongoing uncertainty around the CEO transition.
Potential slowing in customer activity or order levels.
Financial commitments to customers and partners of $518bn, up from $366bn, tie NVDA to the financing of AI infrastructure demand.
Inventory (+26% QoQ) and receivables (+29% QoQ) are growing, with days of inventory and DSO each up 4 days.
The new US Commerce restriction on datacenter rentals to restricted geographies could affect CY27 revenue.
vol_and_positioning: GS describes investor positioning in NVDA as neutral-to-negative, per its conversations with clients, and expects the stock to hold its gains after the print.
GS notes NVDA shares had already been trading at a wide discount to the market on investor concern that AI infrastructure growth could slow without financing from Nvidia or its competitors.
geopolitical: US Department of Commerce newly issued restrictions on datacenter rentals by Nvidia's customers to restricted geographies, including mainland China. Nvidia is still assessing the impact but sees upside to its prior CY27 forecast.
Nvidia is cooperating with all ongoing government investigations related to US export controls and no longer ships permissible Hopper products to China.

tension_points.bull_case: Nvidia says its customer and partner support will stay disciplined and selective, while committing to return all excess cash through about $227bn of buybacks before the end of CY27. GS sees this as a sign management views the stock as undervalued.
tension_points.bear_case: Commitments to customers and partners rose to $518bn from $366bn. GS notes investors worry AI infrastructure growth could slow sharply without financing from Nvidia or its competitors, which is a reason the shares traded at a wide discount to the market.
tension_points.what_invalidates: GS says it will re-examine its view as additional information comes from Nvidia's key customers and from the results of ongoing internal or external investigations. It names no price level or print.

theme_stances.key_argument: Nvidia will keep supporting partners and customers in a disciplined and selective manner while returning all excess cash to shareholders.
theme_stances.evidence: disciplined and selective in its support of neocloud customers

theme_stances.key_argument: Raised CY27 revenue growth guidance to 75% sits ahead of Street expectations, and unconstrained demand remains well in excess of supply.
theme_stances.evidence: unconstrained demand growth for CY27 remains well in excess of supply
